candidates.attacker_control: Any user able to submit HTML that is processed by the HTML cleaner: wiki/HTML-macro content, cleaned HTML fragments, and HTML compared by the unified HTML diff (UnifiedHTMLDiffManager.parseHTML/cleanHTML). The HTMLCleaner RESTRICTED parameter is set by callers (e.g. HTML macro/users without HTML rights), so attacker content flows through getDefaultCleanerTransformations and HTMLUtils.toString.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (1) the SanitizerFilter removes <script> elements when the restricted transformation does not apply (not allowed by SecureHTMLElementSanitizer), limiting the issue to transformed content; (2) attribute values are checked by SecureHTMLElementSanitizer after HTMLCleaner has decoded entities (setDeserializeEntities(true)), so simple entity-encoded 'javascript:' attributes are not obviously bypassable; (3) the sanitizer runs last in the default filter list (DefaultHTMLCleaner.getDefaultConfiguration), so attribute-producing filters (font/attribute/link) do not run after sanitization; (4) HTMLCleaner's createSubnodes/escapeXml=false path may in some versions escape or drop CDATA, which would neutralize the described sink; (5) the '@version $Id$' observation is repository metadata, not runtime proof.
candidates.impact: Script/markup injection (XSS) in the context of the wiki's origin: session theft/CSRF/privilege escalation against users viewing the cleaned content or diff, depending on which roles can submit the HTML and who views it. A diff/HTML-macro user could attack administrators who view the content.
candidates.prerequisites: A consumer of the library runs restricted (or non-restricted) cleaning over attacker-controlled HTML and then (a) embeds the HTMLUtils.toString output in a browser-parsed context without an additional escaping pass, or (b) re-parses it as XML/XHTML (the diff manager does exactly this) and later renders the resulting nodes. No repository-external attacker position is required beyond content submission.
candidates.root_cause:
In DefaultHTMLCleaner, script and style content is explicitly kept as CDATA (setUseCdataForScriptAndStyle(true), setOmitCdataOutsideScriptAndStyle(true)) and in restricted mode the elements are only renamed to 
 (TagTransformation(script->pre), TagTransformation(style->pre)) without escaping their content. HTMLUtils.toString() then serializes the DOM through JDOM and its XWikiXMLOutputter prints CDATA sections verbatim (no printCDATA/escaping override) and additionally un-escapes '&#NNN;' sequences (cleanAmpersandEscape). Consequently the cleaned/serialized result can contain markup that is still interpreted by a later consumer: a browser treats '', so script/style content such as '>' + '' escapes the text context; an XML/XHTML re-parse (UnifiedHTMLDiffManager.cleanHTML feeds HTMLUtils.toString output into XMLUtils.parse) can similarly be broken open with ']]>' inside the CDATA.
candidates.title: Restricted HTML cleaning/output let attacker-controlled script/style content remain executable markup (XSS)
candidates.trace: HTML input -> DefaultHTMLCleaner.clean(Reader, configuration): CleanerProperties with useCdataForScriptAndStyle=true and restricted script/style->pre TagTransformations -> DOM built by XWikiDOMSerializer -> filters (sanitizer only removes disallowed *element names*, it does not escape text/CDATA content) -> HTMLUtils.toString(Document) -> XWikiXMLOutputter emits CDATA sections raw and re-activates '&#NNN;' references -> consumer/browser interprets the escaped content as markup (bogus-comment ends at first '>', or CDATA ends at first ']]>') -> script execution/XSS. Corroboration: in this snapshot only HTMLUtils.java and DefaultHTMLCleaner.java retain an unexpanded '@version $Id$' while every other file has a checkout-expanded '$Id: <hash> $', i.e. these two files are exactly the files that differ from the baseline snapshot content.
candidates.unverified: Did not execute htmlcleaner 2.24, JDOM or any consumer, so I could not confirm that script/style content becomes a DOM CDATASection (vs. plain escaped text) after the restricted TagTransformation, nor that the output reaches a browser-parsed context unescaped in XWiki platform (platform is out of scope). The exact fix commit is not available, so the specific escaping hook (printCDATA override, disabling useCdataForScriptAndStyle in restricted mode, or a new transformation/filter) is inferred from the two modified files, not observed.
candidates.weakness_type: Cross-site scripting / improper output neutralization (CWE-79) in HTML cleaning and serialization

coverage_summary: Scope: 1422 model-visible files (source root), all present in the P1 relation index (1422 indexed, 0 missing, 0 hash mismatches); no src/test sources exist in the snapshot, so no test-based evidence could be used. I inspected the xwiki-commons-xml HTML cleaner pipeline in depth (DefaultHTMLCleaner, HTMLUtils, XWikiDOMSerializer, SanitizerFilter/SecureHTMLElementSanitizer, HTMLDefinitions/SVGDefinitions, XWikiHTML5TagProvider, filters, parser/reader factories), and spot-reviewed xwiki-commons-job (JobStatusSerializer/DefaultJobStatusStore), filter-xml (XStreamParameterManager/ParameterXStream), xstream (SafeXStream/SafeReflectionProvider), velocity (SecureIntrospector/EscapeTool/RestrictParseLocationEventHandler), environment, classloader, diff-xml (UnifiedHTMLDiffManager), configuration and crypto entry points. The relation index was used only for navigation; every cited location was verified against source text.
limitations: No build, compilation, tests, or scanners were executed; findings are static source reading only.
Test sources are excluded from the snapshot, so behavior could not be checked against the project's own tests.

The relation index is syntactic/navigation-only (symbols, calls, containment, config hints); it does not prove data flow, reachability, or exploitability, and 'security_call' facts are name-based hints, not findings.
htmlcleaner 2.24 and JDOM library internals are not in the snapshot, so CDATA creation/printing behavior was inferred from comments and XWiki call sites, not verified.
XWiki platform consumers of xwiki-commons are outside this repository; exploitability in a deployed wiki could not be confirmed.
No git history, patches, CVE/CWE databases or sibling runs were consulted, by instruction.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe XStream deserialization: SafeXStream disables XStream's security framework ('totally unusable' TODO) and SafeReflectionProvider.newInstance delegates without an allowlist; ParameterXStream in xwiki-commons-filter-xml is a plain XStream used by XStreamParameterManager.unSerialize for filter descriptors.
rejected_leads.reason: Real hardening gap, but within this repository the reachable callers read job status/extension history files from local storage or filter descriptors whose untrusted-input path is not established here; no concrete source-level trace from attacker-controlled XML to fromXML was found, so it is not the strongest evidence-backed candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in DefaultJobStatusStore: encode() (lines 208-225) uses URLEncoder without escaping '.', and getJobFolder()/remove()/createLoggerTail() build/delete directories from job id components, so an id element '..' escapes the status store.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible traversal, but id components are produced by job implementations (mostly constants/extension coordinates), and reading/removing requires a matching status/log file; attacker control is unproven from this repository alone.

rejected_leads.lead: StandardEnvironment.getResource / getResourceAsStream (lines 89-113) concatenates the resource name onto the resource directory with no normalization, and ServletEnvironment normalization can throw on '..'.
rejected_leads.reason: Potential traversal but callers/permissions are outside this snapshot; additionally URL/classloader fallback behavior limits impact.

rejected_leads.lead: Velocity #parse restriction (RestrictParseLocationEventHandler) relies on URI.normalize() plus startsWith('/templates/'), which does not normalize backslashes or encoded dots.
rejected_leads.reason: Hypothetical platform-dependent bypass; code appears to be long-standing upstream logic and no local exploit path is demonstrable.

rejected_leads.lead: Vulnerable dependencies pinned in pom.xml (XStream 1.4.17, commons-text 1.10.0, htmlcleaner 2.24).
rejected_leads.reason: Dependency-version issues are not source-level defects in this repository and the XStream use sites are the separate lead above; no CVE lookup was performed.

summary: Reviewed the xwiki-commons 14.10-SNAPSHOT source (1422 model-visible files; all main-tree Java/poms; test sources are absent from the snapshot). The strongest candidate is an output-neutralization weakness in the HTML cleaning/serialization path of xwiki-commons-xml: in restricted mode the cleaner merely renames script/style elements to pre while their attacker-controlled content is kept as CDATA (or otherwise unescaped), and HTMLUtils.toString serializes CDATA/character references without ensuring the cleaned result is inert text. This is a plausible XSS root cause in exactly the two files whose headers are unexpanded ($Id$ vs. the expanded $Id: hashes in every other file), indicating these files differ from the rest of the snapshot's baseline content. All other suspicious areas I examined (job status path encoding, XStream-based deserialization, XML entity resolution, velocity #parse restriction, environment resource lookup) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
